messages:
maria gonzalez: FYI — last night around 02:14 UTC euw1 dedicated pool approached OOM for several shards. root cause looks like KV cache blowup combined with cross-AZ egress spike. opening thread to capture timelines and mitigation notes.

samir: seeing the alert now. do we have the alert link? :eyes:

ops-bot: [ALERT] euw1-dedicated-pool memory_pressure HIGH (02:13 UTC) — affected nodes: 5, pods throttled: 12. svc: inference-dedicated. alert-id: /alerts/12345

ravi_p: quick timeline:
- 01:58 UTC: nightly eval-campaign starts (large batched evals from partner)
- 02:05 UTC: KV cache hit-rate spikes, cache size grows ~3x per-node
- 02:12 UTC: pod-level memory > 92% on 5 nodes, kubelet eviction thresholds hit
- 02:14 UTC: kube-scheduler reschedules -> increased cross-AZ egress as pods bounce
- 02:16 UTC: transient latency and token drop for a subset of tenants

leo: logs I grabbed: ```
[02:12:35] model-worker: kv_cache.size=128M -> 410M in 6min
[02:12:40] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 28911 (model-worker) score 987
[02:13:02] kubelet: Evicting pod inference-abc-123: memory_pressure
```

anya: that cache growth looks like unbounded prefix caching from the eval suite. are they pinning long conversations?

maria gonzalez: yes, eval campaign uses long seqs and repeats similar prefixes across many requests. prefix dedupe isn't kicking in because requests come from different tenants IDs -> cache key includes tenant.

samir: immediate mitigations we applied: 1) increased eviction aggressiveness on affected nodes (temp), 2) applied node cordon for 2 worst nodes, 3) rolled a lightweight config change to set per-tenant cache soft limit to 200MB via feature-flag.

ravi_p: can confirm: after soft-limit rollout at 02:28 UTC memory stabilized. but we saw elevated inter-AZ egress while pods were rescheduling — that amplified network egress costs and increased latency briefly.

leo: rough cost note: additional egress during the incident ~= 1.9TB egress across euw1 in the 30m window (~$1200 estimate) — we should include that in post-incident cost analysis.

anya: three learnings so far:
1) per-tenant cache isolation and soft limits are critical for multi-tenant eval traffic.
2) scheduler placement should avoid overpacking when memory pressure is near threshold (we're currently bin-packing strictly on GPU util).
3) reschedule storms cause cross-AZ traffic spikes; we need smarter pod bounce strategies.

samir: engineering fixes proposed:
- enforce per-tenant cgroups for worker processes (memory.limit_in_bytes)
- default cache TTL for eval route to 30s and explicit max entries per-tenant
- change placement policy to include memory headroom heuristic (prefer spreading when >80% memory used)

ravi_p: ops-level mitigations: add preflight check in autoscaler to avoid scaling-in that would trigger eviction storms; implement exponential backoff for pod restarts to reduce synchronized reschedules.

leo: infra ask for capacity planning: we need to model bursty eval workloads in our GPU-hour forecasting. current forecasting only captures mean production traffic; it underestimates large but short-lived eval campaigns. suggestion: keep a separate "campaign headroom" bucket sized by 99.9 percentile of observed campaign spikes.

maria gonzalez: agree. also suggestion to track KV cache growth per-tenant in telemetry. add a metric: tenant.kv_cache_bytes and an alert when any tenant > 75% of soft_limit.

ops-bot: action created: INC-2026-78 "euw1 eval campaign KV cache protections" assigned to ravi_p (due 2026-03-25).

anya: small config note: for dedicated pools we can expose a tenant-level config to opt-out of long prefix caching if they run evals — will contact partner to apply conservative settings next run.

samir: short-term: propose reducing default batch sizes for eval route and enable prefix dedupe across tenant when origin app id similarity score > 0.95 (cheap heuristic).

ravi_p: long-term: consider adding a distributed global cache controller that enforces tenant quotas at ingress rather than letting worker process cache unbounded. requires design but prevents per-node runaway.

leo: on forecasting — I'll run a sensitivity analysis: how many reserved GPUs would we need to prevent similar incidents for 99.5% of campaign patterns vs changes in batching TTLs. will post numbers here in 24h.

maria gonzalez: good. also add runbook item: when memory alerts spike, do NOT immediately scale-in; instead drain a node, inspect kv_cache metrics, and apply soft-limits then allow autoscaler to rebalance.

anya: tagging for docs: put mitigation steps and telemetry queries into the runbook and add a short playbook for marketing/partners who trigger large evals (require contact before massive batch runs).

samir: follow-ups assigned:
- ravi_p: implement per-tenant soft-limit + alerting (PR in progress)
- leo: forecasting sensitivity + cost calc for egress and reserve vs burst handling
- anya: partner comms + route config change for evals

maria gonzalez: thanks all. if anyone has additional logs or traces from 02:00-02:30 UTC drop them here. otherwise we'll reconvene after the action items. :white_check_mark:

leo: I uploaded a small query to dashboards: `sum by (tenant) (max(kv_cache_bytes) )` with time window 02:00-02:30. link: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/q/kv-spike

ravi_p: quick snippet we used to patch soft-limit in the configmap: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  worker.yaml: |
    caching:
      per_tenant_soft_limit_bytes: 209715200 # 200MB
      default_ttl_seconds: 30
```

samir: note for PMs: we should surface campaign-run risk in the console when users schedule large evals (show estimated memory and egress impact and suggest enabling conservative cache mode).

anya: adding that to product backlog.

maria gonzalez: closing note: root cause = multi-tenant unbounded KV cache growth during a high-parallel eval campaign + scheduler reschedule storm causing cross-AZ egress spike. mitigations agreed and actions assigned. will update INC ticket with this thread summary.

ops-bot: INC-2026-78 updated: status -> triaged, owner -> ravi_p, comments -> "per-tenant soft-limit rolled to production and monitoring added"

samir: thanks folks. :raised_hands:
